summary: Dixie range lights on Lake St. Louis, west of Montreal, established 1915; the front light became Dixie Sector Light in 2018 and the rear tower was dismantled in 2019.

light.note: Coast Guard list: sectors red 110-052 degrees, white 052-050, green 050-263 (current Dixie Sector Light)

structures.note: Enclosed white wooden tower, 40 ft above water (LighthouseFriends quoting the 1915 Lake Carriers' Association report); replaced by sector light August 2018
82 ft tower to top of ventilator; dismantled July 2019 (LighthouseFriends, Coast Guard confirmation)

events.note: Steamer Keefe touched in the main channel 200 feet south of gas buoy 98 S on 6 June 1903; the report gives the buoy's move as about 300 feet in one passage and 100 feet in another
Three Lake St. Louis lightships withdrawn; the seven lights at the lower end put under the Lachine keeper
Two fixed white catoptric range lights established 1 September 1915 (Lake Carriers' Association report, as quoted by LighthouseFriends)

Rear range light's steel skeleton tower dismantled July 2019; warning light placed on its pier

corrections.why: The Coast Guard list gives the Dixie Sector Light sectors of red, white and green, not only red. The record also lists an OpenStreetMap 'Q G' value that the Coast Guard list does not support.

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends says a sector light replaced the front range in August 2018, and the Coast Guard list gives the sector light as current. The station was not deactivated.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's active status is supported: the Coast Guard list gives the Dixie Sector Light as current, and LighthouseFriends says the range remains active. The 2018 and 2019 events are replacements and a dismantling, not the end of the station.

notes_for_editor: 1) Shape and colour: LighthouseFriends describes a cylindrical tower and quick-flashing green lights (cite 1). The Coast Guard list gives a square skeleton tower with a white cylindrical daymark and an isophase light, Iso R W G 6s, with red, white and green sectors (cite 2). The story reports both; a site check would settle it. 2) The 1915 Lake Carriers' Association passage is second-hand, as quoted by LighthouseFriends; the original report was not read. 3) The 1903 report gives two figures for the move of gas buoy 98 S: about 300 feet in the 'Buoys and beacons' passage (scan p. 63, printed p. 50) and 100 ft in the later passage on boulders (scan p. 109, printed p. 96). The story gives both. 4) Matched by column position: the 1916 Dixie row (scan p. 58, printed p. 51) reads 'Dixie / Erection of range lights, front, wooden tower, back, steel skeleton tower / Day labour / J. D. Weir / 7,923 05'. The work and amount are on the Dixie line, and the amount agrees with LighthouseFriends' $7,923.05. The OCR puts the foreman and the amount in separate columns, and the story does not use the foreman's name from this table. The page image has not been viewed; the checker should look at scan p. 58 before the $7,923.05 figure is relied on. 5) Keepers Albert LeBlanc, Ed. Massie and H. Massie come only from LighthouseFriends' 'Head Keepers' line and salary text. The corpus keeper lists searched for 1915-1918 (LeBlanc, Dixie) carry no Dixie keeper line, so the names are not confirmed by the Department's tables. 6) The Department's 1915 Montreal-district list (scan p. 55, printed p. 48) names Dixie among aids with 'Erection of range lights (Work will be completed next year)' in another column; not used. 7) Corrections: the record's 'Iso R 6s' omits the red, white and green sectors on the Coast Guard list (cite 2); its 'Q G' value comes from OpenStreetMap and is not on the Coast Guard list. The record's 2018 'deactivated' event is a replacement by a sector light (cite 1, cite 2), not a closure. The record's boat_only flag is not supported by the LighthouseFriends page, which describes a land view from Parc du Millenaire; left unchanged here. 8) The 1903 Keefe touched bottom (the report's word) and was not a wreck; it sits in the 'Storms, wrecks and rescues' chapter and is recorded as an 'other' event. 9) The Department's 1904 report says the lightship keepers' services were dispensed with; it does not give a date of removal beyond the year ended 30 June 1904. 10) The story's structure: the hazard paragraph moved from 'The place' into a new 'Storms, wrecks and rescues' chapter, in the order the guide gives for light stations.
